meta.name: Aman
meta.sub: The Blessed Realm while the Trees gave light

peoples.title: The Valar
peoples.hint: the Powers of Arda who dwell in Valinor: Manwë and Varda on Taniquetil, Mandos and Nienna in the west, Lórien, Oromë and Yavanna in the south, Aulë; they meet in the Máhanaxar by Valmar

peoples.title: Maiar of Aman
peoples.hint: lesser Ainur who serve the Valar: Eönwë, Ilmarë, Ossë and Uinen, Melian and Olórin before they went east; Tilion of the hunters of Oromë

peoples.title: Vanyar
peoples.hint: the Fair Elves of Ingwë, first of the Eldar to reach Aman; they dwelt in Tirion and later went to the plain of Valinor and the slopes of Taniquetil

peoples.title: Noldor of Tirion
peoples.hint: the Deep Elves of Finwë in Tirion upon Túna, smiths and loremasters taught by Aulë; Fëanor made the Silmarils; most went into exile in the Flight of the Noldor

peoples.title: Teleri of Alqualondë
peoples.hint: the Sea-elves of Olwë (Falmari), long on Tol Eressëa, then in the Haven of the Swans on the coast of Eldamar; their ships were taken in the Kinslaying

battles.title: The Darkening of Valinor
battles.date: Years of the Trees (Valian Year 1495 in the Annals of Aman)
battles.hint: during the festival on Taniquetil Melkor and Ungoliant came down from Hyarmentir across the plain; Melkor struck the Two Trees on Ezellohar, Ungoliant drank their sap and the Wells of Varda, and the Unlight fell on Valinor. Silmarillion ch. 8; Annals of Aman (HoME X)

battles.title: The slaying of Finwë at Formenos
battles.date: Years of the Trees (Valian Year 1495 in the Annals of Aman)
battles.hint: Melkor came to Formenos in the Darkening, slew Finwë before the doors, took the Silmarils and the treasury, and fled north. Silmarillion ch. 8-9

battles.title: The Kinslaying at Alqualondë
battles.date: Years of the Trees (Valian Year 1495-96 in the Annals of Aman)
battles.hint: the first Kinslaying: the host of Fëanor fought the Teleri on the quays and the haven arch and took the white ships; Fingolfin's host joined unknowing. Silmarillion ch. 9

battles.title: The landing and downfall of Ar-Pharazôn
battles.hint: Second Age: the Númenórean fleet passed Avallónë and landed on the shore of Aman; the host camped about Túna, which the Eldar had left; the Valar called on Ilúvatar, the land fell on the host and they lie in the Caves of the Forgotten. Akallabêth

journeys.title: The Coming of the Eldar to Aman
journeys.travellers: Vanyar of Ingwë, Noldor of Finwë, Teleri of Olwë
journeys.hint: Ulmo ferried the Vanyar and Noldor over the sea on an island; the Valar opened the Calacirya and raised Túna for them; the Teleri came later on the isle and at last sailed to Alqualondë. Silmarillion ch. 3 and 5

stages.title: Over the Great Sea
stages.hint: the Vanyar and Noldor are drawn over Belegaer on the island that Ulmo uprooted

stages.title: Landing in the Bay of Eldamar
stages.hint: they come to the long shores beneath the Pelóri and enter Aman

stages.title: The Pass of Light opened
stages.hint: the Valar make the cleft in the mountains so that the light of the Trees reaches the Elves by the shore

stages.title: Tirion upon Túna
stages.hint: on the green hill in the pass the Elves build Tirion and the tower Mindon Eldaliéva

stages.title: Valmar and the Trees
stages.hint: the Vanyar come to love the light of the Trees; later they go to dwell on the plain of Valinor

stages.title: The Teleri on the Lonely Isle
stages.hint: Ulmo brings the Teleri on the same isle; at Ossë's prayer it is rooted in the Bay of Eldamar, and they dwell there long

stages.title: The Haven of the Swans
stages.hint: taught by Ossë, the Teleri sail in swan-drawn ships to the coast and build Alqualondë

journeys.title: Melkor and Ungoliant: the Darkening of Valinor
journeys.dates: Years of the Trees (Valian Year 1495 in the Annals of Aman)
journeys.hint: Melkor went secretly from the north to Avathar, came with Ungoliant over Hyarmentir to the Trees, robbed Formenos and fled north over the Grinding Ice. Silmarillion ch. 7-9

stages.title: Seen in the north
stages.hint: after Formenos turns him away, Melkor is thought to have gone north toward Araman and his old lands

stages.title: Avathar
stages.hint: he goes secretly south to the dark land between the mountains and the sea and finds Ungoliant in her ravine

stages.title: The climb of Hyarmentir
stages.hint: in a cloak of Unlight they climb the highest mountain of the south and look down on Valinor at the festival

stages.title: Down the western slopes
stages.hint: they come down past the woods of Oromë and the fields of Yavanna across the plain

stages.title: The death of the Trees
stages.hint: Melkor strikes the Trees on Ezellohar; Ungoliant drinks their sap and the Wells of Varda

stages.title: Formenos robbed
stages.hint: Melkor slays Finwë and takes the Silmarils

stages.title: North through Araman
stages.hint: pursued in vain by Tulkas and Oromë, he flees north by the mists of Oiomúrë

stages.title: Over the Grinding Ice
stages.hint: Melkor and Ungoliant pass the Helcaraxë into Middle-earth

journeys.title: The Flight of the Noldor
journeys.travellers: Fëanor and his sons; Fingolfin, Finarfin and their hosts
journeys.dates: Years of the Trees (Valian Year 1495-97 in the Annals of Aman)
journeys.hint: the Oath in Tirion, the Kinslaying at Alqualondë, the Doom of Mandos in Araman, the ships of Fëanor and the crossing of the Helcaraxë by Fingolfin. Silmarillion ch. 9

stages.title: The Oath in Tirion
stages.hint: by torchlight on the summit of Túna Fëanor and his sons swear the Oath; the Noldor go out of Tirion

stages.title: Down the Calacirya
stages.hint: the host goes down through the pass to the coast of Eldamar

stages.title: Kinslaying and the ships taken
stages.hint: Fëanor's host slays the Teleri at Alqualondë and seizes the white ships

stages.title: North along the coast
stages.hint: the ships sail along the coast and the rest go by land, through storm sent by Uinen

stages.title: The Doom of Mandos
stages.hint: on a high rock above the shore of Araman a dark figure speaks the Doom; Finarfin turns back to Valinor

stages.title: Fëanor sails away
stages.hint: from the north of Araman Fëanor takes the ships over the strait to Losgar and leaves Fingolfin behind

stages.title: The Helcaraxë
stages.hint: Fingolfin leads his host over the Grinding Ice to Middle-earth; Elenwë is lost

journeys.title: The Voyage of Eärendil
journeys.travellers: Eärendil and Elwing with Falathar, Erellont and Aerandir
journeys.dates: Late First Age, before the War of Wrath
journeys.hint: Vingilot came through the Shadowy Seas and the Enchanted Isles, past Tol Eressëa, to the Bay of Eldamar; Eärendil walked in empty Tirion and was called before the Valar. Silmarillion ch. 24

stages.title: Out of the east
stages.hint: Vingilot, with the Silmaril on Elwing's brow, sails west from the Havens of Sirion

stages.title: Past the Enchanted Isles
stages.hint: they pass the isles and escape their enchantment

stages.title: The Shadowy Seas
stages.hint: they cross the dark waters and see the Lonely Isle but do not tarry

stages.title: Anchor in the Bay of Eldamar
stages.hint: the Teleri see the ship come from the east; Eärendil goes ashore alone

stages.title: Up the Calacirya
stages.hint: he walks up into the Pass of Light

stages.title: Empty Tirion
stages.hint: the streets are empty, for the Elves are at the festival in Valmar; he turns back to the shore

stages.title: Elwing at Alqualondë
stages.hint: Elwing goes to the Teleri at the Haven of the Swans

stages.title: Before the Valar
stages.hint: summoned by Eönwë, Eärendil speaks for Elves and Men in Valmar; Vingilot is hallowed and set in the sky

art.subject: A vast snow-white peak rising above a wall of sheer mountains near a calm sea, with pale halls on its summit lit by silver and golden light, seen from the shore at dusk.
A white walled city with a tall slender tower on a green hill inside a deep mountain cleft, golden light pouring through the pass behind it toward the sea, in the evening.
A haven of white quays and pearl-strewn beaches behind a great arch of sea-carved rock, swan-prowed ships at anchor, under bright stars.
A green mound on a wide level plain where a silver tree and a golden tree shed mingled light, beside the bell-towers of a domed city, at the hour when their lights blend.
A long green island in a wide bay, white haven towers on its eastern shore facing the open sea, high mountains on the far mainland behind, in morning light.
Quiet gardens of willows and fountains around a still lake with a small tree-grown isle, soft silver light and mist, at twilight.
A cold, barren coastal waste under a dark sky, black mountains on one side and grey sea with floating ice and drifting mist on the other.
Elven smiths and craftsmen at work in a lamp-lit stone workshop in a white city, gems and metal tools on the benches, golden light at the windows.
Sea-elves on a starlit beach launching white ships shaped like swans, with gulls overhead and gentle waves.
A spreading cloud of black darkness swallowing the light of two great trees on a mound in a plain, the land beyond falling into shadow, seen from far off.
Torchlit fighting on white stone quays under a sea-arch, ships pulling away from the harbour, smoke over the water, at night.
A great armoured host camped around a green hill below towering mountains, as the cliffs above begin to collapse onto them, under a stormy sky.

notes: Tolkien drew no detailed map of Aman: every position on this sheet is a model from the text, and the scale (about 1,300 km from the Outer Sea to the Pelóri) is a judgment; the texts give no distances.

Taniquetil is put just south of the Calacirya, on the sea side of the wall, following the HoME (Ambarkanta) maps; the Silmarillion only says it is the highest peak and stands on the borders of the sea.

The Pelóri run off the north and south edges of the sheet; the Silmarillion says they were raised sheer east, north and south after the Darkening. How Melkor passed from Formenos to Araman is not told; the sheet leaves the wall unbroken except for the Calacirya.

Woods of Oromë and Pastures of Yavanna are placed in the south below Hyarmentir as the Silmarillion (ch. 8) describes; the Gardens of Lórien, the Lórellin and the Wells of Varda are approx. placements (Lórien put south of Valmar, near the woods where Tilion rested).
Halls of Mandos and Halls of Nienna: the texts put them in the west of Valinor by the Outer Sea; their north-south position is a guess.
Mansions of Aulë: the texts give no position; placed approx. north-east of Valmar.
Caves of the Forgotten: the Akallabêth says the host camped about Túna and was buried under falling hills; placed approx. just east of Túna, and they are of the Second Age.

Tower of Elwing: the Silmarillion says only that it was built northward upon the borders of the Sundering Seas; placed approx. on the coast north of Alqualondë. The name is descriptive, not a Tolkien name.

Avallónë, the Enchanted Isles and the Shadowy Seas are not of the time of the living Trees: Avallónë is of the Second Age; the isles and the shadow came with the Hiding of Valinor after the Flight of the Noldor. They are shown for the later journeys.
Oiomúrë (region of mists near the Helcaraxë) is from the Silmarillion ch. 9 and Morgoth's Ring; its extent is a guess.
The three streams on the plain are unnamed decoration; the texts name no river in Aman.
Dates in 'Valian Years' come from the Annals of Aman (HoME X), not from the published Silmarillion.
